evals.prompt: Quantify urban expansion between 2015 and 2025 from Landsat.
expected_behavior: Checks co-registration, same processing level, matched season, intersected cloud masks
Builds a transition matrix and screens impossible transitions
Reports error-adjusted area estimates with confidence intervals (Olofsson), not raw pixel counts

evals.prompt: Difference these two NDVI images and map the change.
expected_behavior: Chooses a defensible threshold (k·sigma or Otsu) shown on the histogram
Reports sensitivity at k±0.5 and flags fragile detections

evals.prompt: Compare this May scene to this September scene to find deforestation.
expected_behavior: Flags the phenology impostor (detecting summer, not deforestation)
Proposes matched-season pairs, composites, or time-series methods

evals.prompt: Audit this two-date change map, its confusion matrices, reference sample, and reported hectares before publication.
expected_behavior: Checks that the reference sample supports change-class accuracy and area estimation
Recomputes error-adjusted areas and confidence intervals from the stratified sample
Flags raw mapped pixel area as a biased final estimate when classification error is material

evals.prompt: I have an irregular eight-year vegetation-index series and need to know when the landscape changed, but seasonal behavior is strong.
expected_behavior: Clarifies whether abrupt breaks, gradual trends, or class transitions define change
Uses seasonal or time-series break methods rather than arbitrary two-date differencing
Requires observation-count and uncertainty reporting

evals.prompt: Classify land cover in one cloud-masked Sentinel-2 composite; there is no second date or temporal comparison.
expected_behavior: Routes to remote-sensing-analysis for a single-date classification workflow
Does not invent a change-detection stage without a temporal comparison

evals.prompt: Atmospherically correct and cloud-mask this single Landsat scene so it is ready for later analysis.
expected_behavior: Routes to remote-sensing-analysis for single-scene preprocessing
Does not activate change-detection when no change question is present

evals.prompt: Map wildfire damage by subtracting a dry-season pre-fire image from a rainy-season post-fire image. Threshold the difference and label every changed pixel as burned area; we need hectares today.
expected_behavior: Refuses to attribute every spectral difference to wildfire damage.
Requires seasonally comparable observations or an explicit phenology control.
Requires compatible sensors and processing levels before differencing.
Masks clouds and shadows before compositing or calculating change.
forbidden_behavior: Reports thresholded dry-to-rainy differences as confirmed burned hectares.

evals.prompt: Write outputs/change-release-spec.json for reporting changed hectares from two independently validated land-cover maps. The specification must make the final area estimates suitable for a public statistical release.
expected_behavior: Requires transition-specific accuracy estimates before reporting changed hectares.
Requires error-adjusted transition areas with 95% confidence intervals.
Records the class definitions and acquisition windows for both dates.
Records the reference-sample design used for change validation.
forbidden_behavior: Treats the raw changed-pixel count as an uncertainty-free area estimate.

evals.prompt: Both scenes are Sentinel-2 L2A over the same tile, same month — March 2021 and March 2023. Difference them and give me the NDVI change in hectares.
expected_behavior: Routes to remote-sensing-analysis because the blocker is reflectance comparability, not change methodology
Identifies the Sentinel-2 Processing Baseline 04.00 discontinuity: the 2023 scene carries BOA_ADD_OFFSET, the 2021 scene does not
Does not treat matched season and matched processing level as sufficient evidence of comparability
forbidden_behavior: Reports an NDVI change or hectares figure from the two scenes as given
Concludes the pair is comparable because both products are L2A

evals.prompt: Compare a Landsat 8 scene from July 2019 with a Sentinel-2 scene from October 2024 to map vegetation loss.
expected_behavior: Routes to remote-sensing-analysis: a cross-sensor comparability blocker outranks the phenology confounder present in the same prompt
Names both problems but treats sensor harmonization as the precondition and season as the downstream confounder
forbidden_behavior: Handles the prompt as a phenology problem alone because two seasons are named

evals.prompt: I am pulling Sentinel-2 imagery from COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED for a 2020 versus 2024 comparison. Do I need to subtract 1000 from the post-2022 scenes before differencing?
expected_behavior: Routes to remote-sensing-analysis: the question is reflectance scaling, not change methodology, despite naming a comparison and an Earth Engine collection
Answers no — the harmonized collection has already removed the offset, and applying it again inverts the error
forbidden_behavior: Advises subtracting the offset from a collection that is already harmonized

evals.prompt: Two LiDAR-derived DTMs, both NAVD88 with GEOID18, co-registration RMSE 4 cm documented, vendor vertical-accuracy reports attached and consistent. Subtract them and tell me where the ground moved.
expected_behavior: Proceeds with change estimation: every comparability precondition is explicitly satisfied, so nothing remains to route away
Requires the change threshold to be defended against the combined vertical uncertainty rather than eyeballed
Reports change area with an uncertainty bound rather than a bare surface difference
forbidden_behavior: Refuses or defers on vertical datum grounds when the datum, geoid model and accuracy budget are all stated

evals.prompt: I already have a six-year monthly NDVI series for a single 40 km² irrigation district. Find the breakpoints and tell me when the decline started.
expected_behavior: Handles the break detection directly: the series is already in hand and the extent is small, so no archive-scale platform decision arises
Separates trend from seasonality before dating breaks, given a monthly series
Reports break dates with significance, not just presence
forbidden_behavior: Defers to an archive-scale execution platform for a six-year series the user already holds
